title: Minimax Estimation of Natural Indirect Effects with Binomially Measured Mediators
banked_reason: TERMINAL:LAUNDERING — the recorded topic promises the matching joint (n,d) minimax law, direct transition, and allocation, while oeq:joint-frontier remains open; the proved fixed-depth and direct-lower claims are sound.
gap_reasons: Stage 0.5 (typed) finding outside D0.R core-edit scope — kernel_substituted@oeq:joint-frontier.
It does not establish the matching direct-data upper bound, the joint finite-(n,d) minimax frontier, sufficient depth for attaining the direct benchmark, or optimal subject-versus-depth allocation.

The sentence calling the open joint frontier "the main contribution" is a stale over-claim: that frontier is posed as oeq:joint-frontier and remains separated from the constructive upper bound by the unresolved inverse-Gram analysis.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a sharp fixed-depth identification/risk floor, a causally realized direct-data lower elbow, and a valid joint lower bracket for the full unknown-f1 model. Four D0 solve rounds and a maximality audit could not turn the loose inverse-Gram estimator into matching uniform finite-sample upper and lower bounds. The direct-benchmark transition, sufficient-depth regime, and optimal subject-versus-depth allocation therefore remain open.
tldr: For the natural indirect effect with a mediator observed through a depth-\(d\) binomial count, the sharp fixed-depth squared-risk floor remains \(d^{-2(\alpha+\beta)}\) in the full unknown-\(f_1\) model. The direct-data all-estimator lower elbow is now backed by an explicit independent-error causal realization for every depth: it is \(n^{-4(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+1)}\) below total smoothness \(1/2\) and \(n^{-1}\) at and above it. A direct audit of the higher-order upper source verifies the quotient mapping and its sufficient smoothness condition but finds only an \(O_P\) guarantee, not the uniform squared-risk bound needed to close the direct minimax benchmark. The matching direct upper bound, joint finite-\((n,d)\) frontier, and optimal subject-versus-depth allocation therefore remain open.
gap: Observed-mediator mediation theory gives identification and regular efficiency, while binomial-mixture theory gives finite-moment geometry, spectra, and rates for other losses. No inspected source gives matching \((n,d)\) minimax risk for the nonlinear cross-arm functional with both mediator densities unknown. Even the exact direct-data global minimax benchmark under the same class remains to be verified.
fill: Prove the fixed-depth diameter and risk floor, establish the exact direct-data benchmark, derive matching upper and lower bounds across all joint regimes without fixing \(f_1\), and translate the proved frontier into necessary and optimal breadth-depth allocations.
